sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
As informed by learned AGA, notice to the informant has been served on 01.04.2025 but none is present on behalf of the informant.

2. Heard Ms. Pratibha Jaiswal, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Deepak Kumar Singh,
learned A.G.A. for the State and also perused the material placed on record.
3.

Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 74 of 2024, under Sections 376(3), 376(2)N of IPC and Sections 3/4(2), 5J(ii)/6, 5L/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station - Myorpur, District - Sonbhadra, during the pendency of trial.
4. As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have committed rape with the minor daughter of the informant, aged about 14 years, between 01.12.2023 to 31.12.2023.

The victim had not Maya Ram Gond vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20405674/
1 revealed the matter to anyone out of shame but the matter surfaced as the victim got impregnated and the said pregnancy was visible to one and all.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged in the FIR.
The FIR is delayed by about eight months and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
The applicant is a distant son-in-law of the informant and he has never visited his house.

6. Learned counsel has also stated that the families of the father-in-law of the applicant and the informant are at loggerheads with each other, as such, the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The statement of the informant has been recorded in court denying the institution of the FIR and disclaiming any involvement in its transcription.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 12.08.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
7. Per contra, learned AGA has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the victim was of tender age i.e. 14 years old only and she got impregnated and she has nowhere to go.
The applicant is the cousin brother-in-law (Jeeja) of the victim and he misused his clout and committed the said offence.
The consent, if any, of the victim pales into insignificance owing to her tender age, as such, the applicant is not entitled for bail.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties, the age of the victim and the relationship with the applicant, I do not find it a fit case to release the applicant on bail.

9. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected.
10.

However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously, in view of the principle laid down in the recent judgements of the Supreme Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.

sentences.text: 11. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
12. The counsel for the applicant persisted in arguing the matter despite the judgment being dictated, and refused to leave the dais.
This unprofessional conduct is unacceptable.
13. Consequently, I hereby impose a fine of Rs. 1000/-, which shall be deposited by the counsel into the account of the High Court Legal Services Committee within a week.

14. Place this application on 23.04.2025 in the daily cause list among top ten cases for compliance only.
